title: Affine chart criterion and Zariski locality for scheme local quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]; (2) for every pair of affine opens $A\subseteq X$, $B\subseteq S$ with $f(A)\subseteq B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the induced ring map $\mathcal O_S(B)\to\mathcal O_X(A)$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and quasi-finite at every prime of $\mathcal O_X(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]; (3) there are open coverings $S=\bigcup_jB_j$ and $f^{-1}(B_j)=\bigcup_iA_{ji}$ such that every restriction $A_{ji}\to B_j$ is locally quasi-finite. No finiteness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01TK (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-characterize), equivalences (1), (2), (3); quasi-finite ring maps mean finite type and quasi-finite at all target primes.

proof.text: Assume (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], f is locally of finite type, and [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] therefore makes the induced map on any affine pair A,B of finite type. Let q be any prime of the coordinate ring of A and let x be the corresponding point. The definition [pqf-def-quasifinite] says that f is quasi-finite at x. The existing characterization [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] makes the point of the fibre over f(x) isolated. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] to this x and the given affine pair A,B gives that the same ring map is quasi-finite at q. Thus it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 01TK, proof of (1) => (2), using Tag 01TH and Tag 01T2.

proof.text: Assume (2) and fix x in X. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open B around f(x), and then an affine open A around x contained in f^{-1}(B). Condition (2) applied to A and B supplies a finite-type ring map which is quasi-finite at the prime corresponding to x. By the definition [pqf-def-quasifinite], this makes f quasi-finite at x. Since x was arbitrary, f is locally quasi-finite, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 01TK, proof of (2) => (1), with affine opens supplied by Schemes Tag 01IT.

proof.text: Assume (1). Choose an affine open cover S=⋃_j B_j using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. For each j, apply the same basis statement to the open subscheme f^{-1}(B_j) to obtain an affine open cover f^{-1}(B_j)=⋃_i A_{ji}. The restriction [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] of a locally quasi-finite morphism to these open subschemes is locally quasi-finite, so every A_{ji}->B_j is locally quasi-finite. This is (3).

source.place: Tag 01TK, proof of (1) => (3), together with Tag 01TH (4) and Schemes Tag 01IT.

proof.text: Assume (3) and let x be any point of X. Choose j with f(x) in B_j and then i with x in A_{ji}. Since A_{ji}->B_j is locally quasi-finite, [pqf-def-quasifinite] supplies affine neighbourhoods inside these opens whose induced ring map is finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of x. The same neighbourhoods are open subschemes of X and S, so they witness that f is quasi-finite at x. Hence f is locally quasi-finite, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 01TK, proof of (3) => (1), by unpacking Definition 01TD on the covering pieces.

lean.statement: theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_affine_criterion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : (f.IsLocallyQuasiFinite ↔ ∀ (A : X.Opens) (B : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen A → IsAffineOpen B → ∀ e : A ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ B, ∃ hft : (f.appLE B A e).hom.FiniteType, ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, A), @Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime Γ(S, B) Γ(X, A) _ _ (f.appLE B A e).hom.toAlgebra hft q) ∧ (f.IsLocallyQuasiFinite ↔ ∃ (J : Type u) (B : J → S.Opens) (I : J → Type u) (A : ∀ j : J, I j → X.Opens) (e : ∀ (j : J) (i : I j), A j i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ B j), (⨆ j : J, B j) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ j : J, (⨆ i : I j, A j i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ B j) ∧ ∀ (j : J) (i : I j), (f.resLE (B j) (A j i) (e j i)).IsLocallyQuasiFinite)
